title: SSE: tenant-aware keepalive, session rehydration, and orphan-fragment reconstruction
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Multiple customers reported truncated real-time responses from the Hosted API SSE endpoint after intermediate network blips. Symptoms include: clients receive a short valid prefix, then silence for 10-30s, then a reconnect where the server emits a continuation that the client cannot attribute, resulting in duplicated or missing tokens in the user-visible transcript. Incidents observed across edge proxies in front of the runtime (Envoy variants) and across both shared-hosted capacity and a customer on Dedicated. This ticket investigates tenant-aware keepalive heuristics, a lightweight session rehydration mechanism to permit deterministic continuation after reconnect, and a playbook to reconstruct orphaned fragments when attribution fails.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long-running generate request via SSE against hosted.redwood.example/api/v1/stream with max_tokens=2048 and client-supplied session_id header (SDK-enabled).
2) During early token emission (50-200 tokens), simulate a 5s TCP stall at the edge (iptables DROP) or kill an Envoy worker to induce a perceived SILENCE, then restore connectivity.

3) Client reconnects using same session_id and last_seen_offset header; server may emit new events that are treated as a new session by the edge or client SDK, causing duplicate prefix or a gap in final transcript.

4) Observe logs and telemetry: missing session checkpoint entries in Redis, edge attributing events to a new connection id, and mismatch between final token sequence numbers emitted and what client merged into transcript.
observed_behaviour: Short valid prefix followed by silence (no SSE comment heartbeats)
On reconnect, server emits continuation frames that are not reconciled with earlier partial transcript
Telemetry shows high per-tenant reconnect rate and increased duplicate token counts in transcript QC metrics
Some Dedicated customers see similar issues when fronting load balancers swap backends during maintenance windows
hypothesis_and_root_causes: Edge proxies drop or coalesce SSE keepalive comments, leaving SDKs unable to distinguish a transient stall from full termination
No tenant-aware keepalive: global health heuristics treat all sessions the same which leads to aggressive server-side eviction of ephemeral checkpoints
Checkpointing is too coarse: last_checkpoint only recorded per-request completion or large intervals, losing mid-stream continuation state
Clients that do not send client-generated session tokens (older SDKs) cannot be reliably reattached to the original in-memory session
Race between stream worker eviction and reconnect: worker reaped, new worker starts producing a separate transcript fragment
logs_and_artifacts: Customer report: Zendesk #43218 (AcmeRetail) with attached client logs and SDK trace IDs
design_proposal: 1) Tenant-aware keepalive injection: emit lightweight SSE comment heartbeats that include tenant_id hash and connection_epoch so downstream edge proxies can avoid coalescing or dropping them. This helps the SDK detect a true termination vs transient stall.

2) Ephemeral mid-stream checkpointing (session rehydration): write compact session checkpoints to Redis with TTL (default 90s) containing: last_emitted_token_index, RNG seed, kv-cache pointers, and minimal request metadata. Keep writes rate-limited and delta-encoded to avoid IOPS blow-up.
3) Client-labeled session tokens: SDKs will emit a client-generated session_id if available; server will prioritize reattachment by session_id then by tenant+last_seen_offset heuristics.

4) Reconstructor playbook for orphan fragments: when a reconnect arrives without a checkpoint, attempt best-effort reconstruction by correlating trace IDs, per-token checksums, and recent worker logs. Emit audit events and a reconciled transcript suggestion to the client SDK for manual merge if deterministic reassembly is impossible.
5) Telemetry: add new metrics 'session_rehydrate_hits' and 'orphan_fragment_reconstruct_attempts' and dashboards for per-tenant rates and success ratios.
6) Backward compatibility: default to current behavior unless tenant sets 'enable_session_rehydration' via project config; flip for impacted customers while running a broader rollout.
risk_assessment: Redis write amplification if checkpointing frequency is too high — mitigate with delta encoding and batching
Edge behavior variance — some proxy versions may ignore SSE comments; we must fallback to server-only heuristics
Potential small latency increase on reconnect path due to rehydration lookup (expected <15ms with colocated Redis)
Wrong reattachment could cause duplicate text; mitigation: conservative matching and emitting 'suspected-dup' flags for client SDK to dedupe
acceptance_criteria: Instrumented tenant-aware heartbeat emitted for every SSE stream and validated by unit/integration tests
Session checkpoint created at safe delta intervals and rehydration succeeds for >=95% of simulated edge stall reconnections in our chaos tests
Reconstructor can produce a reconciled transcript suggestion for >=70% of historical orphaned fragments in customer sample traces
New telemetry available in Grafana and alerts for session_rehydrate_fail_rate > 5% per tenant
Documentation and SDK changes published: SDK adds opt-in client session_id header and de-duplication logic
implementation_notes: Runtime: add a lightweight checkpoint writer that writes a delta blob to Redis with TTL. Use pipelined writes and optional compression. Feature gate behind runtime-1.22 and runtime config 'session_rehydrate'.
Edge: coordinate with infra to ensure Envoy config preserves SSE comment frames and doesn't coalesce them under keepalive timeout. Add a canary route for impacted tenants.
SDK: add session_id generation and last_seen_offset tracking. Client merges server 'suspected-dup' flags by preferring first-seen tokens unless deterministic checksum matches continuation.
Ops/playbook: include steps to manually trigger reconstruction for a tenant using 'reconstruct_stream' admin tool and to toggle the feature per-tenant via flags service.

F) Customer communication: prepare runbook and ticket template for Customer Success to use while feature is toggled for remediation (owner: CS)
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Decided to prefer short-lived Redis checkpoints rather than persisting to durable store to reduce cost and complexity (decision maker: Eng Leads)
2026-03-11: Keep client session_id opt-in for now to avoid breaking older SDKs; target full default rollout after 2-week canary (decision maker: Product)
2026-03-12: Telemetry and conservative matching prioritized for initial rollout; automatic aggressive reattachment deferred to later cycle
